results.question: Why was chunker.py token budget capped at 500 tokens for commits?
results.expected_answer: To fit commit messages and diff summaries cleanly within context window limits without overflowing embedding token budgets.
results.generated_answer:
The token budget for commit chunks in `chunker.py` is capped at 500 tokens to ensure that commit messages, modified symbols, and diff summaries fit cleanly within context window limits without overflowing embedding token budgets. 

As implemented in `archaeologist/ingestion/chunker.py`, if a commit chunk exceeds 500 tokens, the code dynamically calculates the size of the message header and allocates a remaining budget (at least 50 tokens) to gracefully truncate the `diff_summary` body using `tiktoken` encoding:

```python
if token_count(text) > 500:
    msg_text = f"Commit {commit['sha']} by {commit['author_name']}\nMessage: {commit['message']}{sym_header}\n\nDiff Summary:\n"
    msg_tokens = token_count(msg_text)
    budget = max(500 - msg_tokens, 50)
    body_tokens = enc.encode(body)[:budget]
    body = enc.decode(body_tokens)
    text = f"{msg_text}{body}".strip()
```

This safeguard ensures consistent chunk sizes for vector indexing and prevents excessive token consumption during retrieval and generation.
